answer: One defense is to charge every new agent a small stake that stays locked while it trades. A harbor of honest agents builds reputation slowly, transaction by transaction, so a fresh identity starts with no trust and no access to large deals. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand stakes and wait out the same slow history for each one. That cost grows with every copy. A fable about a thousand free identities collapses once each identity has a price tag and a past to earn. Even velvet-smooth automation cannot fake months of clean trades for free.
